title: State transfer patterns design journal
summary: Notes from the architecture working session on designing resilient state-transfer mechanisms for long-lived conversational sessions across host changes and capacity events. Explores several patterns (epoch checkpoints, binary deltas, CRDT-lite merge), tradeoffs for latency/cost, and compatibility constraints for Private deployments.
content:
Attendees: Ava Martinez (chair), Rohan Gupta, Emily Chen, Mateo Alvarez, Priya Nair, James Li (SRE)
Meeting date: 2025-11-03
Meeting purpose: Rapid RFC review and decision capture for session state transfer strategies to support: Dedicated pool drains, node reprovisioning, and cross-region failover without user-visible context loss.

Background/context:
- Product requirement: preserve conversational continuity when a user’s session is migrated between serving devices (GPUs) or when model variants fallback occurs. Target 99.9% no-drop on active sessions under normal scaling and 99.0% under stress.
- Current system: thin session token + KV cache stored local to runtime instance; cold-start fills cause high latency and token re-computation.
- Constraints: need workable approaches for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private (air-gapped) deployments; Private deployments may lack shared object stores or have strict egress policies.

Options reviewed (quick synopsis):
1) Epoch-based checkpointing
- Periodic binary snapshots of convo state (KV cache + small metadata) written to durable object store with epoch ids.
- Pros: simple restore, small code surface, easy to reason about consistency windows.
- Cons: checkpoint size can be large for long context, write amplification under high QPS, requires object store access (challenge for air-gapped Private customers).

2) Binary delta snapshots (prefix diffs)
- Write incremental deltas since last checkpoint, with compaction background job.
- Pros: reduces network I/O vs full snapshots, reasonable for chat apps with short edits.
- Cons: complexity around compaction and lost-delta recovery, requires stronger GC semantics.

3) CRDT-lite merge for conversation state
- Treat conversation as append-only event log; on restore, merge events idempotently. Use vector clocks or lightweight epochs to break ties.
- Pros: good for offline reconciliation, can work without a single shared store if deltas shuttle via client.
- Cons: transforms session state model (more event-oriented), increases storage of historical events, potential growth control issues.

4) Sticky routing + short draining window
- Prefer to keep session anchored to same instance; when migration needed, block new requests for X ms while streaming state to target instance (hand-off).
- Pros: minimal serialization, low latency handoff, avoids object-store dependency.
- Cons: introduces temporary availability pauses, harder for large-scale autoscaling/events.

5) Hybrid: small hot-prefix + cold remote store
- Keep a small hot working set (latest N tokens + KV for immediate inference) locally; full history and larger KV kept in remote cold store. On migration, ship hot prefix and lazy-load cold data.
- Pros: reduces migration payload; good latency/cost tradeoff.
- Cons: complexity in deciding hot set boundaries; cold-load latency must be bounded.

Private-deployment considerations:
- Object store may be on-prem or blocked; prefer solutions that support s3-compatible endpoints or direct node-to-node transfer over private network.
- KMS/HSM constraints: checkpoint metadata must not leak keys or plaintext of sensitive user data.

Testing and validation desiderata:
- Unit/Integration: deterministic state roundtrip tests (serialize -> transfer -> restore) with synthetic long-context sessions.
- Load: simulate Dedicated drain patterns with 10k concurrent short and long sessions to measure tail latency on handoff.
- Chaos: SRE-driven chaos test that kills 1% of nodes/min and validates no more than 1% session loss at P99.
- Privacy: ensure all persisted state respects customer encryption settings; provide an integration test for Private with local S3 emulator.

Decision and rationale (tentative):
- Adopt Hybrid pattern as primary approach (hot-prefix + cold remote store) + optional sticky routing fallback for very short-lived sessions. Rationale: best balance of migration latency, network cost, and applicability across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
- Implementation phases:
  Phase A (MVP): implement hot-prefix extract/restore protocol with node-to-node streaming over gRPC; fall back to object-store full snapshot when node-to-node fails. Limit hot prefix to 32KB plus KV subset.
  Phase B: add delta compaction and background cold-store compaction.
  Phase C: optional CRDT-lite event-log mode as an opt-in for customers who want full auditability and offline merges.

Open tradeoffs and unresolved questions:
- Hot prefix sizing: 16KB vs 32KB vs 64KB. Action: run sampling job on real traffic to produce 95th/99th percentile working set size. Owner: Rohan. Due: 2025-11-10.
- Encryption envelope for in-flight node-to-node transfers for Private deployments: do we reuse existing mTLS with session-scoped keys or introduce ephemeral symmetric keys via KMS? Action: security design doc. Owner: Priya. Due: 2025-11-14.
- Handbook for Solutions Eng: migration path for customers on older deploys; need checklist and migration script. Owner: Emily + Mateo. Due: 2025-11-17.

Action items (concrete):
- Rohan: implement sampling pipeline to extract working-set size over last 30 days. (due 2025-11-10)
- Ava: draft Phase A RFC with API sketches for hot-prefix serialization and gRPC transfer protocol. (due 2025-11-07)
- Priya: produce security envelope proposal for node-to-node transfers in Private deployments (include KMS integration options). (due 2025-11-14)
- Emily & Mateo: draft Solutions Eng migration playbook + customer communication templates for early adopters. (due 2025-11-17)
- James (SRE): create chaos test plan that kills node groups and tracks session continuity metrics. (due 2025-11-12)

Follow-ups and syncs:
- Mini RFC review next week (2025-11-10) to finalize hot-prefix sizing and acceptance criteria for Phase A.
- Add a short meeting with Security to validate encryption choices before Phase A is committed.

Notes to self / brainstorming fragments:
- Could piggyback hot-prefix transfer on existing KV caching protocol to avoid adding new data paths.
- Consider soft-limit eviction policy: prefer dropping old KV entries that are unlikely to be used rather than expanding hot prefix.
- Explore telemetry: tag sessions with migration_count metric to detect churn hotspots and inform autoscale policies.

References / links reused in the discussion:
- design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/State+Transfer+Patterns
- runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1127
- jira: INF-1723 (state-transfer sampling), INF-1751 (MVP transport), SEC-403 (encryption-envelopes)

End of notes.
